posts.heading: November 12, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 21 species on November 12, with 18 heard, 10 seen, and 7 both, across 53 feeder visits. That is well below the past week's average of 91.0 visits, while the 238 detections ran above the 221.1 average, and the species count of 21 sat close to the 21.6 average.

Northern Cardinal, Eastern Towhee, Carolina Wren, Tufted Titmice, American Crow, Blue Jays, Carolina Chickadees, Northern Mockingbird, Song Sparrow, and White-throated Sparrow were all recorded on each of the past seven days, including this one. Eastern Phoebe and Mourning Dove, both recorded on earlier days this week, were not recorded today. No species was seen or heard at this station for the first time today.

The audio source was switched many times during the day, moving between the pi, c120, and pi-mic (movo-dom1) inputs, and each detection comes from whichever source was active at the time. The higher detection total should therefore be read with that mixed setup in mind rather than as more birds present.

posts.heading: November 11, 2026
posts.text:
The day was quieter than the past week, with 34 feeder visits against a seven-day average of 126.0 and 160 detections heard against 216.9. Twenty species were recorded, close to the average of 22.1. Northern Cardinal led with 38 detections heard and 3 seen, and Red-shouldered Hawk (24 heard) and Eastern Towhee (20 heard) were also prominent.

Eleven species recorded on every one of the past seven days, including this one, held again: American Crow, Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Carolina Wren, Eastern Phoebe, Eastern Towhee, Northern Cardinal, Northern Mockingbird, Song Sparrow, Tufted Titmouse, and White-throated Sparrow. Ruby-crowned Kinglet returned after its last record on 2026-11-04, seen once as a probable. White-breasted Nuthatch, recorded on six of the previous seven days, was not recorded today, and no species was new to the station.

The audio source was switched repeatedly between the pi, pi-mic (movo-dom1), and c120 sources from 04:35 to 07:30, so the heard counts draw on mixed sources. The first visual record was a Northern Cardinal 4 min before sunrise, and the last was a Blue Jay 452 min after sunrise, 172 min before sunset.

posts.heading: November 10, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to a quieter one at the feeders, with 36 visits against a seven-day average of 129.6, while 21 species was close to the usual 22.3 and 213 detections was near the 218.0 average. Northern Cardinal led on both sides, with 8 confident visits and 28 detections. The first visual was Tufted Titmouse 31 min after sunrise, and the last was Northern Cardinal 634 min after sunrise, 8 min after sunset.

Eleven species were recorded on each of the last seven days, including this one: American Crow, Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Carolina Wren, Eastern Phoebe, Eastern Towhee, Northern Cardinal, Song Sparrow, Tufted Titmouse, White-breasted Nuthatch, and White-throated Sparrow. Hermit Thrush returned after 11 days away, with its last earlier record on 2026-10-30 and one detection today. Gray Catbird, Red-bellied Woodpecker, and American Goldfinch were recorded earlier in the week but not today.

The audio source was switched many times through the day, from 05:20 until 23:58.

posts.heading: November 9, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday the station logged 17 species, 16 by ear and 7 by sight, with 6 both heard and seen across 63 feeder visits. That was quieter than the past week on every measure, against averages of 22.3 species, 131.3 visits and 236.0 detections. The first confident visual was a Carolina Chickadee 23 min before sunrise, and the last was a White-breasted Nuthatch 315 min after sunrise, 313 min before sunset.

Eleven species were recorded on all seven days, including yesterday: American Crow, Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Carolina Wren, Eastern Phoebe, Eastern Towhee, Northern Cardinal, Song Sparrow, Tufted Titmouse, White-breasted Nuthatch and White-throated Sparrow. Eastern Towhee led the day with 33 detections, and Northern Cardinal logged 7 confident visits. House Finch, recorded on each of the six previous days, was not recorded yesterday.

American Robin was heard for the first time at this station, with 10 detections, after being away for 15 days since 2026-10-25. The audio source was switched repeatedly over the past week and again during yesterday, so these are ear detections from whichever microphone was active, not a visual arrival. A Ruby-throated Hummingbird was logged once as a probable visit earlier in the week, and yesterday had no new confident visual species.
